notes: Primary research article (experiment plus DFT), so not theoretical_only and not not_primary. Hydrogen enters as H2/D2 adsorbed on gas-phase fullerene ions in helium nanodroplets; adsorption is read as the ion-abundance anomaly at n = 32 (C60+) and 37 (C70+), not as an amount taken up by a bulk sorbent, and the paper states 'we cannot control the temperature' (main, article p. 074311-12, Section VIII Conclusions). H2 partial pressure is given only as 'typically a few times 10-3 Pa (uncorrected gauge signal)' (main, article p. 074311-2, Section II Experiment). No H2 uptake value, no surface area. The only 'surface area' mention is generic ('porous, light-weight materials with large specific surface areas', Introduction). record.json is_retracted is false and no retraction notice in the text. No statement that the data were published before (the paper cites its earlier letter, Ref. 12, but does not say its values are repeated). The three non-criterion codes do not apply. I2 to I4 left null per the I1 rule.
